title: BenchmarkRun
description: One measured run of a workload by one side, at one date and build, with the µs per step of each repeat and their median (story:benchmark-history). The median of an odd number of repeats is the middle one in ascending order, of an even number the mean of the middle two.

date.description: The day of the run, `YYYY-MM-DD`; for a figure that only a CHANGELOG release states, that release's date.

workload.description: What was trained, `mnist-784-64-10` (examples/mnist_mlp.mspec on MNIST, batch 100), `mlp-784-H-10` (the `mlp_sweep` bench, 784 → H ReLU → 10 at the batch and hidden width of the run), `transformer-block` (the `transformer_block` bench, examples/transformer_block.mspec at the batch of the run, in sequences of 128) or `bert-tiny-pretrain` (examples/bert_tiny.mspec, MLM pre-training on the packed corpus, 32 sequences of 128, timed to a held-out loss target).

threads.description: The CPU threads of a CPU side, where the source states them.

modelspec_version.description: The ModelSpec release the run was built from, on a ModelSpec side.

commit.description: The ModelSpec repository commit the run was built or run from, as the source states it, full or abbreviated.

opponent_version.description: The opponent's version, such as `torch 2.14.1+cu130`, on an opponent side.

batch.description: The batch of a workload that takes one as a parameter.

hidden.description: The hidden width H of a workload that takes one as a parameter.

tokens_per_step.description: The tokens of one step of a sequence workload, batch times sequence length, such as `1024` for `transformer-block` at a batch of 8 sequences of 128; with it the page shows tokens per second, tokens_per_step · 10⁶ / median_us_per_step.

flop_per_step.description: The FLOP of one step by flop_rule, where the source states it.

flop_rule.description: What flop_per_step counts; present exactly with flop_per_step.

timed_steps.description: The steps of one timed repeat, where the source states them.

repeat_count.description: The repeats the source measured, recorded in repeats_us_per_step or not.

repeats_us_per_step.description: The µs per step of each repeat in the order the source lists them; null when the source states only the median. A source that gives seconds per repeat over timed_steps steps has each value as seconds · 10⁶ / timed_steps.

median_us_per_step.description: The median µs per step of the repeats, as the source states it, or computed from its median seconds as seconds · 10⁶ / timed_steps.

target_loss.description: The held-out loss a time-to-target run trains to; for `bert-tiny-pretrain` the held-out unigram baseline of its packed corpus, `heldout_unigram_baseline_nats` `6.926537926202018` of `packed.json`, which the reference run passed on its way to a final held-out loss of 6.7674994; with steps_to_target, seconds_to_target and eval_every, required on a `bert-tiny-pretrain` run.

steps_to_target.description: The first evaluated step whose held-out loss is at most target_loss, a multiple of eval_every, where the source states it.

seconds_to_target.description: The training seconds up to steps_to_target, the cumulative `train_seconds` of that step's eval line, without the held-out evaluations, checkpoint writes or events (`modelspec train --clock`, and the opponent's eval lines).

train_seconds.description: The training seconds of the whole run, as seconds_to_target counts them.

eval_every.description: The steps between held-out evaluations of a time-to-target run, which bound how finely steps_to_target is resolved.

final_heldout_loss.description: The held-out loss at the run's last step, where the source states it.

gpu.description: The GPU of a GPU side, as the source names it.

driver.description: The GPU driver version, as the source states it.

sm_clock.description: The SM clock during the run as the source states it, in its own words; clocks were not locked.

note.description: What the source says qualifies the figure, such as a loaded host.

source.description: Where the figures are stated, a verification-report id such as `verification-report:mlp-size-sweep-2026-10-23` or a CHANGELOG release such as `CHANGELOG.md [0.6.0]`, followed by `raw records <path>` when the per-repeat values come from records committed under `benchmarks/raw/` that the report does not hold.

modelspec.benchmark.BenchmarkRunId.title: BenchmarkRunId
modelspec.benchmark.BenchmarkRunId.description: The name of one run in `benchmarks/runs.yaml`, unique in the file, such as `mnist-0.6.0-modelspec-vulkan`.

modelspec.benchmark.FlopRule.title: FlopRule
modelspec.benchmark.FlopRule.description: What flop_per_step counts. MatmulOnly counts the matrix products of a step, forward and backward, by workload, `3196·B·H` for `mlp-784-H-10`, the matmuls of a 784 → H → 10 step at batch B, and `N·(42·H² + 24·H·F + 24·S·H)` with `N = B·S`, `H = 128`, `F = 512` and `S = 128`, that is `339,738,624·B`, for `transformer-block` at a batch of B sequences (benches/transformer_block/block.rs), and `N·(54·H² + 24·H·F + 6·H·V + 24·S·H)` with `V = 8,192`, that is `1,170,210,816·B`, for `bert-tiny-pretrain` (benches/bert_tiny/flop.rs); AllSites is the `profile step_total` count over every dispatch site of the step (DESIGN.md § 3.1 counting rule).

modelspec.benchmark.Mode.title: Mode
modelspec.benchmark.Mode.description: Timed is a run measured end to end over its timed span; Profiled is the steady µs per step of `modelspec train --backend vulkan --profile`, with timestamp queries in the run.

modelspec.benchmark.PositiveInteger.title: PositiveInteger
modelspec.benchmark.PositiveInteger.description: A whole number of at least 1, the type of every count and size of a BenchmarkRun (threads, batch, hidden, tokens_per_step, flop_per_step, timed_steps, repeat_count); the generated JSON Schema carries it as `minimum` 1.

modelspec.benchmark.Side.title: Side
modelspec.benchmark.Side.description: Who ran the workload, a ModelSpec backend or an opponent (AGENTS.md, an opponent is a competing implementation under `opponents/`), and how. PyTorchCudaCompile and PyTorchCpuCompile are `torch.compile`; the eager variants are PyTorch without it.
